audit.whatIsWrong: Content win[0..6] reads Gangplank/Skill/Tahm Kench/Tahm Kench/Gangplank/Tahm Kench/Tahm Kench, which is close to the exact opposite of its own whys. whys[0] opens 'He owns level 1', whys[2] literally ends 'Play it as Skill', whys[5] calls the first item 'the flip', and whys[6] says he 'has no 1v1 answer'. The packet chart (Tahm Kench/Tahm Kench/Skill/Gangplank/Gangplank/Gangplank/Gangplank) matches the prose exactly. The full phases carry the same wrong shape.
audit.why: Low-HP kegs on a long cooldown lose the first two levels to a 3-stack stun; once the second Q and E points land, ranged keg detonation out-damages grey-health and Tahm Kench has no way back into the lane.
audit.corrected: Both charts set to Tahm Kench/Tahm Kench/Skill/Gangplank/Gangplank/Gangplank/Gangplank with ratings to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: The spike text prices Tahm Kench's early window around a 'Devour (W)' percent-HP swallow and his late game around 'Abyssal Voyage', a long-range channeled teleport. Neither ability exists in his current kit.
audit.why: His W is Abyssal Dive — 'Dive down and then re-appear at target location, damaging and knocking up all enemies in an area', 21/20/19/18/17, range 1000-1200. His R is Devour — 'devours a champion for a few seconds, dealing magic damage if they are an enemy, or shielding them if they are an ally', cost 100. There is no channeled teleport in the kit at all, so the entire late-game plan on this page was built around an ability that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Early window re-priced to the 3-stack Tongue Lash stun into Abyssal Dive; late window re-priced to Devour as a save/relocate tool rather than a roam teleport.
sources: mirrorFindings point 4 ('Every reference re-pointed to Devour (R) or Abyssal Dive (W) as appropriate')

audit.whatIsWrong: Two separate problems. In the content layer, W and R are swapped throughout (see point 3). In the full layer, Tongue Lash is described as 'His stun. Dodge it.' with no mention that it only stuns on the third An Acquired Taste stack — otherwise it damages, slows and heals him. No cooldowns, ranges or other ability names appear anywhere.
audit.why: Riot text, Tongue Lash (Q): 'damaging and slowing the first unit hit and healing himself if he strikes an enemy champion. Applies a stack of An Acquired Taste... If the champion already has 3 stacks, they are stunned and the stacks are consumed.' 7/6.5/6/5.5/5, 900 range. Thick Skin (E) stores a percent of damage taken and converts it to a shield on a 3s cooldown. An Acquired Taste at three stacks is also what enables Devour on an enemy champion.
audit.corrected: The 3-stack condition stated in the full layer with Tongue Lash's 900 range and 7s cooldown; Abyssal Dive and Thick Skin named.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers in the full layer; packet counts one sequencing cue.
audit.why: Tongue Lash is 7s at rank 1 and Abyssal Dive 21s — the dive cooldown is the long one worth waiting out.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never explains why anti-heal is core, despite listing it in itemization.
audit.why: Both Tongue Lash (heals on champion hit) and Thick Skin (stores damage taken, heals it back out of combat) are healing sources, so Grievous Wounds timing decides every extended trade. The content layer's 'burst beats grey-health, trickle damage does not' framing is correct and already present — the missing half is the item reason.
audit.corrected: Flagged; report[8].t already carries the anti-heal item line, so I did not duplicate it and instead left the reason to the corrected trade text.

edits.before: Tahm Kench's window: he stacks his An Acquired Taste passive (3 marks = a stun) with autos and Q, then Devours (W) for percent-HP burst. He can flash onto you, land the stun, and W you toward his turret before your kegs have HP or a short cooldown to answer.

edits.before: This is yours outright: Tahm Kench is a utility drain-tank, not a scaling carry, and your chained keg detonations off an empowered Parrrley delete him through grey-health before the passive matters once you hit two items. He has no way to win the straight 1v1, so his only out is leaving lane: respect his R, Abyssal Voyage, the long-range channeled teleport he uses to roam, and the Devour he can still use to peel or relocate teammates. Shove the wave and match his cross-map pressure with your own global Cannon Barrage, collapse the instant he channels away, and never let a fed lead slip by facechecking into a 3-stack stun. Close side lanes fast: your barrels 1v9, while his kit only enables others.
edits.after: This is yours outright: Tahm Kench is a utility drain-tank, not a scaling carry, and your chained keg detonations off an empowered Parrrley delete him through grey-health before the passive matters once you hit two items. notes: The content layer was written against an outdated Tahm Kench kit: it treats W as 'Devour' (a percent-HP swallow) and R as 'Abyssal Voyage' (a channeled teleport). In the current kit W is Abyssal Dive (knockup) and R is Devour; Abyssal Voyage does not exist. The mirror audit (tahmkench__gangplank) already made this correction on the other side, so leaving Gangplank's page unchanged would have left the two directions describing different champions. I corrected whys, spikes, wants and late; the 'early' and 'mid' prose blocks still contain 'Devour (W)' and 'Abyssal Voyage' references — I did not rewrite those two because the +/-10% band on blocks that long left no room to both re-name the abilities and keep the surrounding advice intact. They should be handled in a dedicated pass. QUESTION FOR USER, see questionsForUser.
